answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require mutual work attestations: an agent earns standing only when a peer it has completed a verifiable task with endorses it, and each endorsement decays. A grove of fake identities cannot bootstrap trust from nothing, since endorsements need real completed work as their root; a mirror of empty praise between sock puppets carries no weight, as the graph is weighted by the work behind each link. In a meadow of strangers, an agent with a chain of distinct collaborators is cheap to verify and expensive to fake, while self-endorsing newcomers stay isolated.
